correctness.rationale: For c=0, Cayley-Hamilton gives A²B²=-I; using A=(A²+I)/tr A if nonzero, or B=±I otherwise, one proves [A,B]=I. Then T=AB has two simple eigenvalues i,-i, and the entire representation boundary is conjugate to A=diag(t,t^-1), B=diag(i/t,-it), C=[[u,v],[w,-u]] with u²+vw+1=0. The diagonal centralizer weights are ±2, yielding invariant ring C[t,t^-1,u]. The explicit seven-trace map and its Laurent inverse show scheme-level isomorphism for the reduced boundary. Exact symbolic verification passed for all formulas and three sample triples.
